nuance: Say 안녕히 가세요 to the person who is leaving while you stay. The verb 가세요 means go, so it literally wishes them a safe departure.
mistakes: Saying 안녕히 가세요 when you are the one leaving

english: Goodbye (said by the person who is leaving).
usage: bye, keep up the good work
nuance: Say 안녕히 계세요 when you leave and the other person stays behind. The verb 계세요 means stay, so you are wishing the person who remains to be well.
mistakes: Mixing up 가세요 (you stay) and 계세요 (you leave)

examples: My name is Minsu. Nice to meet you.
nuance: Use 만나서 반가워요 right after introductions in friendly polite settings. It usually follows your name or 안녕하세요, and you can reply with 저도 반가워요.
mistakes: Using it again after the first meeting, not for later visits

english: How do you do (formal first meeting).
usage: how do you do, I am Minsu Kim
I look forward to working with you
examples: How do you do. I am Minsu Kim.
How do you do. I look forward to it.
nuance: 처음 뵙겠습니다 is a very formal greeting for meeting someone for the very first time, common in business. 뵙다 is the humble form of meet, so it shows deep respect.
mistakes: Using it with close friends, where it sounds too stiff

english: I will eat well (said before eating).
examples: Wow, looks tasty. I will eat well.
Thanks for the meal. I will eat well.
I will eat well. I will start.
nuance: Say 잘 먹겠습니다 just before you start eating, especially when someone treats or cooks for you. It thanks the host in advance and politely signals you are about to begin.
mistakes: Saying it after the meal instead of before

examples: It was really tasty. I ate well.
I ate well. Next time is on me.
nuance: Say 잘 먹었습니다 right after finishing a meal to thank whoever provided or cooked it. It is the natural counterpart to 잘 먹겠습니다 and works like saying that was a great meal.
mistakes: Forgetting the past form and saying 잘 먹겠습니다 after eating

examples: Long time no see. Have you been well?
It has really been a long time.
nuance: Use 오랜만이에요 when you meet someone you have not seen for a while. It is friendly and polite, and people often follow it with 잘 지냈어요? to ask how the person has been.
mistakes: Using it with people you saw recently

examples: Long time no see. How are you doing?
How have you been these days?
I am doing well. And you, Minsu?
nuance: 어떻게 지내요? asks how someone has been living lately, not just this moment. It often follows 오랜만이에요, and a common reply is 잘 지내요 (I am doing well).
mistakes: Confusing it with 어디 가요 (where are you going)

nuance: Use 축하해요 to congratulate someone on good news in friendly polite settings. You often place the occasion in front of it, as in 졸업 축하해요 (congrats on graduating).
mistakes: Using it for sad events instead of happy ones

examples: It is your birthday, right? Happy birthday!
nuance: 생일 축하해요 is the everyday way to wish a happy birthday to friends and peers. For elders use the honorific 생신 축하드려요, since 생신 is the respectful word for birthday.
mistakes: Using 생일 instead of honorific 생신 for elders

english: Thank you for your hard work.
examples: Thank you for your hard work today.
The meeting is over. Thanks, everyone.
I will head out. Keep it up.
nuance: 수고하셨습니다 thanks someone for finished effort, so use the past form when work is over. Use the present 수고하세요 to someone who is still working, often as you leave.
mistakes: Saying 수고하셨습니다 to clearly senior bosses, where it can sound improper

nuance: 잘 자요 means sleep well and is used at night with friends and peers. For elders use the honorific 안녕히 주무세요, since 주무시다 is the respectful verb for sleep.
mistakes: Using 잘 자요 with elders instead of 안녕히 주무세요
